key_insight: Sparse long-range (power-of-two) entangling gates can expand a variational circuit’s accessible operator space, but that extra expressibility does not automatically translate into better trainability or task performance.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware with reconfigurable long-range connectivity, circuit geometry itself becomes a resource that should be matched to the target problem rather than assumed beneficial by default.
method: Dynamical Lie-algebra analysis of reachable operator space
Approximate unitary-design diagnostics to test expressibility
Finite-depth measures of entanglement and expressibility plus benchmark variational tasks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons across example problems with and without long-range coupling, using algebraic and finite-depth diagnostics to evaluate how sparse graphs change expressibility, entanglement, and optimization behavior.
watch_item: Greater connectivity may increase circuit flexibility without improving optimization, so hardware overhead and problem matching should be checked before adopting sparse long-range gates.
paper_title: Variational Learning with Sparse Long-range Entangling Gates
